referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A parked vehicle prop: an exterior shell with no interior geometry, since a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside and the glazing is authored as a tinted, mostly opaque pane. The wheels are the mechanisms: each is a named pivot on its axle. Nothing else moves and nothing attaches, so there are no sockets. A high-roof passenger minibus of the intercity van terminals. The plate shows a white van with a short nose, a steep windscreen, a tall roof with an air-conditioning pod, four glass bays a side (door glass then three windows), a sliding door, a red-teal-blue belt stripe, grey bumpers and steel wheels with road dust low.

reasoning: The identity is the side profile -- short blunt nose, straight steep screen into one long roof dome, high monobox roof with a rounded AC pod, three side windows behind the door glass -- and it is one closed polygon swept across the width, with the wheel arches cut into it as notches, then narrowed above the belt for tumblehome. One geometry carries the whole shell.
One repetition system: four wheels off one lathe, each a named pivot on its axle.
A colour difference is not a material difference: every trim tone -- tyre, rim, bumper, lamp -- is a vertex colour on one white material, and the paint carries its dirt as a canvas.
Action readiness is the wheels: four hinge pivots, convex collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A vehicle cannot be a box on a box: the raked screen, the tumblehome and the arches are what make it read at prop distance, and all three come from shaping one extrusion. The glasshouse is a second extrusion of the cab polygon offset 6 mm proud so no pane shares a plane with the body. The roof carries an AC pod; the belt carries a three-colour stripe and a sliding-door rail. SECOND PASS: the sweep is subdivided 14 across the width and FILLETED -- a 0.28 m roof shoulder from the tail to the top of the door glass (faded out by z 1.80), a 0.42 m plan radius at the nose and 0.12 at the tail, a bulged r 1.20 m screen over the bumper into a r 2.25 m roof dome, a 0.30 m rear roof corner, the AC pod its own rounded extrusion -- with angle-limited (50 deg) smooth normals; the pillars are side strips beside the panes, not slabs across them. FOURTH PASS: black window gaskets, a dark lower valance, a sky-gradient glass tile, dusty dark steel rims, the dust as a smooth film and the stripes faded as the plate has them.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 1.88 x 2.28 x 5.38 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=8000 triangles, <=6 draw calls, <=4 materials, <=8 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus one named pivot per wheel (4); zero sockets; convex collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

silhouette.description: Sill 0.40 m, wheels 0.66 m in diameter at z +1.64 and -1.47 (3.11 wheelbase, 1.05 front overhang), a blunt nose with a 0.12 m bonnet lip to a scuttle at 1.22 m at z 2.44, a bulged r 1.20 m screen from there to 1.86 m at z 2.10 (7 cm of bulge, wrapping round a 0.42 m plan nose radius to the A-pillars), a r 2.25 m roof dome to 2.12 m by z 1.05, flat to z -2.39, a 0.30 m rear roof corner into a vertical tail at z -2.69; AC pod 0.86 x 0.80 m to 2.27 m. Section: 0.96 W at the belt (1.25 m) narrowing 20 percent to the roof with a 0.28 m shoulder, roof flat 0.47 W.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -0.94..+0.94 on the shell (mirrors to +-1.06); y 0.00 to 2.25 at the roof AC pod; z -2.69..+2.69 bumper to bumper, +Z forward. The Meshy proxy normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.479 : 0.366 (2.09 lengths tall against the declared 2.36; width 0.366 L = 1.97 m against 1.88), so heights are proxy fractions of H and stations fractions of L at the declared metres.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.479 : 0.366, i.e. 5.38 x 2.58 x 1.97 m at the declared length -- 13 percent taller than the registry, the proxy having read the plate's high viewpoint as height. Heights are proxy fractions of H: roof 1.00, belt 0.55, wheel top 0.29, sill 0.18; stations nose 0.03 L, screen base 0.02 L (the user's read, over the bumper; the proxy puts it at 0.05 L), dome to 0.30 L, tail 0.99 L; axles 0.20 L and 0.77 L. Second pass read the proxy side and end depth maps (_ev/side.pgm, end.pgm) column by column: screen top 0.85 H at 0.13 L, roof 0.935 H from 0.30 to 0.90 L, rear corner 0.96..1.00 L; half-width 0.96 at the belt, 0.80 at 0.80 H, 0.55 at 0.92 H, pod 0.45 W.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.75: rear doors with a recessed skin, vertical lamps and a grey bumper, built to type and to the proxy's rear elevation.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/paint.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.716. localOverrides.evidence: Lower flank #8a8985 against the upper #a7a7a7; a smooth wash, 0.16 film, 90 zoned spray streaks and 1,500 specks at that ratio.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-paint (the roof, PBR confidence 0.716) at #d7dadf, the envelope. The dust is darker in every channel -- rear quarter #797979 against the shaded side #9ca0a3 (0.77), sliding door #a5a5a4, lower flank #8a8985 against the upper #a7a7a7 (0.82) -- so the tile paints it as the linear ratio of #b6b4b0 over a white base: solid to the sill (0.17 of a 2.30 m tile), fading out at 0.92 m (0.40), a 0.16 cloudy film, 90 spray streaks and 1,500 specks zoned behind both wheels with the tile fitted to the length, upward faces keyed clean. The third build laid #9a9690 on as 260 streaks and 4,500 specks and rendered the flank #62615f against the plate #8a8985; the plate dust is a smooth film.
Textureless as DECLARED: the dust is a 512 px Canvas 2D mud tile bound after construction as map.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 6,412/8,000 triangles, 4/6 draw calls, 3/4 materials, 4/8 unique geometries, two canvases at 1.7 MB, factory ~150 ms. Colliders hand-padded to the envelope with a front-bumper box and measured: 8 boxes, coverage 0.957.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: 3 components and one repetition system: 4 of 6. The pillars ride the shell; every trim part rides one merge.

materials.note: paint, glass and a white vertex-coloured trim: 3 of 4. Tyres, rims, bumpers and lamps differ in albedo only.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 6,412 of 8,000: one extrusion with two 8-segment arches, a 20-segment wheel lathe, and boxes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A closed side-profile polygon extruded across the width and shaped per vertex (tumblehome above the belt, plan rounding at nose and tail); an offset extrusion of the cabin polygon for the glass; a lathe for the wheel; boxes for everything else.
One InstancedMesh carries the four wheels; the right-side instances are yawed a half turn so the dish faces out. No per-instance colour, so the white base is inert.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. TWO Canvas 2D tiles are bound after construction: a 512 px mud tile fitted to the length as the paint map (dust ratio formed in linear space, zoned behind the wheels) and a 256 px sky-gradient glass tile as the glazing map. 1.7 MB of texture VRAM, factory ~150 ms.
